guideSubtitle: Segregate at source to protect sanitation workers, enable recycling, and earn compliance points.

categories.name: Wet & Biodegradable Waste
categories.description: Organic kitchen and garden materials suitable for municipal composting and biomethanation.
acceptedItems: Fallen leaves, flowers, and garden twigs
Bones, fish scales, and meat scraps
Used coconut shells and sugarcane bagasse
prohibitedItems: Plastic food wrappers and cling film
instructions: Drain excess liquids before disposing into the green bin.
Do not dispose of organic waste in sealed single-use plastic carry bags.
Keep bin lid tightly closed to prevent pest breeding.

categories.name: Dry & Recyclable Waste
categories.description: Non-biodegradable recyclable items intended for registered recyclers and EPR credit logging.
acceptedItems: Rinsed and dried milk pouches and oil packets
Newspapers, magazines, office paper, and shredded paper
Flattened cardboard and corrugated delivery boxes
Aluminium beverage cans and tin food cans
Clean glass bottles, jars, and glassware
Tetra Pak beverage cartons (rinsed and flattened)
prohibitedItems: Food-stained pizza boxes or greasy paper
Broken window glass or mirrors (wrap separately)
instructions: Rinse and dry all plastic packets and drink containers to prevent mold and foul odor.
Flatten cardboard cartons to optimize collection vehicle space.
Keep dry waste clean — wet contamination reduces recycling viability by up to 80%.

categories.name: Domestic Hazardous Waste
categories.description: Toxic, flammable, corrosive, or dangerous household chemicals and sharps.
acceptedItems: Household batteries (AA, AAA, button cells, rechargeable)
Aerosol spray cans, insecticides, and mosquito repellents
Bleach, acid cleaners, and drain uncloggers
instructions: Never dump hazardous fluids down household sinks or storm drains.
Keep original labels on paint cans and chemical containers.
Store batteries in a cool, dry plastic container before handing over.

categories.name: Sanitary & Biomedical Waste
categories.description: Intimate hygiene and wound-care materials requiring sanitary incineration protocols.
acceptedItems: Used bandages, gauze, and medical cotton
instructions: Wrap each item securely in multiple layers of old newspaper or disposal pouches.
Mark the wrapped packet with a prominent red 'X' or dot.
Hand over separately to the sanitation worker — never flush down toilets.

categories.name: Electronic Waste (E-Waste)
categories.description: Discarded electrical and electronic equipment containing valuable metals and hazardous components.
acceptedItems: Old mobile phones, chargers, USB cords, and earphones
Small kitchen appliances (toasters, blenders, electric kettles)
prohibitedItems: Swollen or leaking lithium batteries (handle with caution under hazardous stream)
instructions: Do not attempt to dismantle or smash electronic devices at home.
Remove removable batteries before handing over.
Schedule an on-demand municipal e-waste pickup or drop at authorized EPR depots.

dos: Do segregate into at least 3 distinct bins: Wet (Green), Dry (Blue), and Hazardous/Sanitary.
Do rinse milk pouches, beverage cartons, and food tins before placing in dry recyclables.
Do flatten corrugated cardboard cartons to maximize collection efficiency.
Do wrap sanitary napkins and diapers securely and mark with a red identifier.
Do verify pickup weights with your driver to earn verified compliance points.
donts: Don't mix wet kitchen waste with dry recyclable plastics or paper.
Don't dispose of batteries, paints, or CFLs in regular domestic bins.
Don't flush sanitary products, wipes, or plastics down household toilets.
Don't use unsegregated black plastic garbage bags for municipal door-to-door pickups.
Don't burn leaves, plastic, or waste in open air — it violates municipal bylaws.
